title.value: Handle inbound chat, email and social as a solo founder

introduction.value: A solo founder uses OpenClaw to automate inbound chat, email and social channels, and is trying to set up an executive assistant for research and personal items.

method.value: The founder tried to use OpenClaw in a solo B2B SaaS to automate customer success and inbound communication, giving the agent documentation plus access to the codebase, database, and Stripe. After early success generating detailed customer reports, they kept expanding it, repeatedly rebuilding the setup as things broke, and were also exploring a separate executive-assistant workflow for research, social life, and financial tasks.

outcome.value: It produced reports that would have taken a person hours or days, but the founder says it failed at autonomous customer communication because it wanted to send too much wrong information. After two weeks they shut it down, saying the time spent was not proportional to the output and that heartbeat costs alone could run about $35 per month.

notes.value: The main catch was maintenance and token burn: they say even on a cheap heartbeat model, idle background use still added meaningful monthly cost.

source_text.body:
Handle inbound chat, email and social as a solo founder
A solo founder uses OpenClaw to automate inbound chat, email and social channels, and is trying to set up an executive assistant for research and personal items.
Done with
OC
OpenClaw
What they did
The founder tried to use OpenClaw in a solo B2B SaaS to automate customer success and inbound communication, giving the agent documentation plus access to the codebase, database, and Stripe. After early success generating detailed customer reports, they kept expanding it, repeatedly rebuilding the setup as things broke, and were also exploring a separate executive-assistant workflow for research, social life, and financial tasks.
How it went
It produced reports that would have taken a person hours or days, but the founder says it failed at autonomous customer communication because it wanted to send too much wrong information. After two weeks they shut it down, saying the time spent was not proportional to the output and that heartbeat costs alone could run about $35 per month.
Worth knowing
The main catch was maintenance and token burn: they say even on a cheap heartbeat model, idle background use still added meaningful monthly cost.
Try it yourself
with
OpenClaw
Copy prompt
I run [business description] solo. Connect to my [chat, email and social channels] and triage every inbound message: answer common questions using [FAQ or docs link], tag sales leads, and escalate anything unclear to me. Done means a daily summary of what came in and what you did, and show me any reply you want to send about pricing, refunds or commitments before sending it.
